The differential metabolite panel is most strongly associated with **Galactose Metabolism** (KEGG map00052; FDR=0.0, fold-enrichment=950.9) and its disease counterpart **Galactosemia** (SMP00182; FDR=0.0, fold-enrichment=982.6). Six metabolites anchor this finding: **sucrose (C00089)**, **D-glucose (C00221)**, **myo-inositol (C00137)**, **glycerol (C00116)**, **galactinol (C01235)**, and **galactitol (C01697)** — all confirmed members of both **Galactose Metabolism** and **Galactosemia** according to the pathway membership outputs.

**Key driver compounds.** Galactitol (C01697) and galactinol (C01235) are annotated in Galactose Metabolism (KEGG map00052) and Galactosemia (SMP00182), alongside sucrose (C00089) and D-glucose (C00221). Their coordinated dysregulation is consistent with perturbations in galactose handling, where galactose accumulation drives shunt into alternative metabolic fates including galactitol and galactinol pools. D-Glucose (C00221) is a confirmed member of the same **Galactose Metabolism** pathway, and its perturbation alongside these galactose-derived intermediates suggests redistributed carbon flow within this metabolic network.

**Biological significance.** The coordinated dysregulation of these six metabolites is consistent with impaired galactose-to-glucose interconversion — a hallmark of galactosemia — where galactose accumulates and shunts into galactitol and galactinol synthesis. The concurrent detection of **acetaminophen (C06804)**, **aspirin (C01405)**, and **N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319)** points to an additional **drug/foreign-compound metabolism** axis (Reactome R-HSA-9749641), which may reflect exposure or therapeutic intervention interacting with the underlying carbohydrate metabolism defect.

**Limitations.** The specific biochemical claim that galactinol serves as a galactosyl-donor for raffinose-family oligosaccharide synthesis was not substantiated by the pathway enrichment or membership outputs; accordingly, that enzymatic role description has been omitted.
